newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajikistan mine to produce 1.3 tonnes gold in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Tajikistan mine to produce 1.3 tonnes gold in 1996.

text.p: Production at Tajikistan's Zarafshan gold venture will total 1.3 tonnes this year, a company official said on Thursday.
Production was halted for two weeks over a dispute between the Tajik government and its Canadian partner, Nelson Gold Corporation Ltd a Nelson official said.
"We closed the plant down for two weeks in September because of a dispute with the government," Craig Brown, one of Zarafshan's Canadian directors, told Reuters.
"We resumed operations based on promises from the Ministry of Finance and the prime minister," said Brown, who gave no details of the dispute.
Brown said 1996 production at the joint venture's Jilau (Dzhelau in Russian) mine, with an average grade of two grams of gold per tonne, would total 1.3 tonnes.
Production began in January this year at the mine, located in the north of the mountainous Central Asian nation and far from a four-year civil war which has raged elsewhere in Tajikistan.
He said the mine should be at full capacity of around 2.4 tonnes in 1997.
Nelson has invested $52 million in the project so far, with a further $150 million scheduled, in which development of the Taror field is planned.
Taror's grade is estimated at around six grams per tonne.
